comparison: Both evaluate VSG exchange kinetics (C3, C27-C34). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with well-documented measurements. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the system mimics physiological VSG switching or represents toxic artifact, and whether reversion represents selection of revertants rather than true reversibility.

Both address cell cycle effects (C43-C51). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by multiple complementary approaches. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether phenotypes reflect physiological processes or toxicity from VSG overexpression overwhelming cellular machinery.

Both evaluate global transcription reduction (C52-C56). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by BrUTP incorporation and luciferase reporters. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, citing recent whole-genome studies showing little evidence for global transcription reduction during stumpy differentiation, suggesting effects may reflect VSG121 toxicity rather than physiological development.

Both address PAD1 induction (C69-C72, C143-C144). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with quantified cell cycle specificity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not challenging the data directly but questioning whether the experimental system represents physiological signaling or artifact of non-physiological ectopic VSG expression.

Both evaluate developmental competence (C8, C73-C81, C142, C149-C150, C156). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive data including EP1 expression and morphological changes. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the differentiation competence data without specific concerns.

Both address ESAG specificity (C5-C7, C82-C93, C147). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes incomplete ESAG1 knockdown may underestimate phenotype. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting more information on ESAG functions, noting ESAG5 was not tested, and ultimately requesting abstract modification to state ESAGs 'appear to serve' or 'could serve' as signals.

Both evaluate reversibility (C94-C102, C152-C153, C155). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes low re-induction percentage. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing significant concern about selection for revertants and stating authors provided no evidence that VSG121 can be re-induced, suggesting 'significant problems with the experimental approach.'

Both address directional ES attenuation (C4, C35-C42). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with statistically significant position-dependent kinetics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not directly challenging the data but questioning physiological relevance of the entire experimental system.

Both address T. b. rhodesiense evolutionary hypothesis (C134-C139). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting established facts but speculative interpretation about ESAG loss. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, with broader concerns about physiological relevance undermining confidence in extrapolations to host range.

Both evaluate DOT1B role (C4, C57-C66). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, showing mechanistic separation of VSG silencing from ES attenuation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the differential effects in DOT1B knockout cells without specific concerns.

Both address main conceptual conclusions (C103-C105, C109, C157). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by collective experimental evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating conclusions about ES as 'global regulator' or 'global control module' are not convincing and should be toned down, requiring studies in pleomorphic strains.

Both evaluate VSG-OR system comparison (C9-C12, C106-C108). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting conceptual interest but speculative conservation claims. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging the feedback model itself by citing stable double VSG expressers that contradict the proposed mechanism.

Both address interpretation of incomplete switching (C110-C122, C128-C132). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting interpretations are speculative and built on experimental system whose physiological relevance is questioned.

OpenEval addresses speculative biological significance models (C128-C133) rating UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental support. Peer reviewers address overlapping claims about incomplete switching and probing ES performance, also rating UNCERTAIN with concerns about the foundation of the experimental system.

OpenEval addresses background knowledge and novelty (C19-C26) rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers group broader background claims (C1-C2, C9-C26, C123-C126, C134-C136, C141, C151) rating SUPPORTED as established literature context not challenged.

Both address VSG feedback inhibition model (C67-C68, C103). OpenEval finds DOT1B experiments SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED for the feedback model, citing double VSG expressers that don't impair growth and questioning how the model works when VSGs are co-expressed with ESAGs.
OpenEval addresses fundamental VSG biology (C1-C2, C17-C18) rating SUPPORTED as established knowledge. Peer reviewers include these in broader background claims rated SUPPORTED as literature context.
OpenEval addresses antigenic variation background (C13-C16) rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers include these in broader background claims rated SUPPORTED as foundational knowledge.

OpenEval addresses ESAG properties from literature (C123-C127) rating UNCERTAIN due to speculative functional interpretations. Peer reviewers include these in background claims rated SUPPORTED, not specifically challenging the cited literature.

OpenEval addresses OR system comparison (C9-C12) rating UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers include these in background claims rated SUPPORTED, though they challenge the feedback model comparison elsewhere (R12).

OpenEval addresses main conclusions including C103 rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers separately challenge the feedback inhibition model (C103) rating UNSUPPORTED, citing contradictory evidence from double VSG expressers.
OpenEval addresses T. b. rhodesiense facts (C134-C136) rating UNCERTAIN for evolutionary speculation. Peer reviewers include these established facts in background claims rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval addresses host range speculation (C133) rating UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN for T. b. rhodesiense hypothesis, with broader concerns about physiological relevance.

OpenEval addresses developmental competence claims (C140-C142, C145) rating UNCERTAIN due to unpublished stumpy formation data. Peer reviewers address overlapping C142 in developmental competence evaluation rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval addresses directional attenuation including C4. Peer reviewers address DOT1B experiments including C4, both finding the mechanistic data acceptable though questioning broader physiological relevance.
OpenEval addresses main conclusions including C147 rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address ESAG specificity including C147 rating UNCERTAIN, requesting evidence for ESAG functions.
OpenEval addresses ES attenuation vs SIF-mediated stumpy formation (C151, C154) rating SUPPORTED for reversibility distinction. Peer reviewers include C151 in background claims rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval addresses monomorphic cell developmental competence (C140-C142, C145) rating UNCERTAIN due to unpublished data. Peer reviewers include C141 in background claims rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval addresses distinction between ES attenuation and SIF-mediated stumpy formation (C151-C154), rating SUPPORTED for reversibility but noting speculation about completing ES switching. No corresponding focused peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval addresses developmental competence in monomorphic cells (C140-C142, C145), rating UNCERTAIN primarily because stumpy formation claim relies on unpublished data. No corresponding focused peer review evaluation found, though C141-C142 appear in other peer evaluations.
